body: Saint Pierre and Miquelon is a French overseas department south of Newfoundland, Canada, and counts as France for country streak purposes.
Licence plates are white or yellow, short or long, with a blue EU strip. White plates also have a blue strip on the right, and front plates are optional.
All coverage was taken with a Generation 3 trekker camera.
Most houses are made of wooden panels, featuring a boxy look and often have vivid colours.
The landscape consists of flat or rolling grasslands, and the coast is often visible.
Coverage is limited, found only in eastern Saint-Pierre and the northern tip of Miquelon-Langlade.
Miquelon-Langlade is a small town with houses having timber cladding painted in bold, vivid colours. A shadow of the ATV used for coverage is also visible.
Saint-Pierre, the capital, has a more populated feel with larger buildings and cars. The coverage is from a sidewalk trekker.
Île-aux-Marins features a slightly hilly, grassy landscape with boxy houses spaced apart.
The rural trekker in the far north features a rolling, grassy landscape and a wooden path with trees on either side.
The rural trekker on Saint Pierre island has a more rocky landscape and a path with trees on both sides.
The boat trekker between Saint Pierre Island and Île-aux-Marins is recognizable by a man wearing a grey and black sweater.
